title: Northgate Care Protection Plans Claim Acceptance and Covered Failures
content:
**Acceptance.** A claim on a Northgate Care Protection Plans contract is taken only on a plan whose status is active. A claim is accepted only when it is filed no later than the plan's claim reporting period in calendar days after the failure date. Days are counted as calendar days, the failure date being day 0. The failure date must fall between the plan's coverage start date and its coverage end date. Claims are filed through the plan's claim channel.

**Covered failures.** Covered failures are exactly those the plan's coverage switches name: mechanical and electrical failures where the plan covers them, power surges where the plan covers them, drops and spills where the plan covers accidental damage, the stain types the plan lists where the plan covers stains, and structural failures — including body impressions at least as deep as the plan's mattress sag depth — where the plan covers structural failure. A built-in battery holding less than the plan's battery capacity threshold counts as failed where the plan covers batteries, and a display with at least the plan's dead pixel count counts as failed. Cosmetic damage, normal wear, consumable parts and damage present before coverage are excluded as the plan's switches say, and commercial use is covered only for products bought on a business-segment membership where the plan covers commercial use for business members. A failure of any other type is denied.

**Where service takes place.** Televisions with a screen of at least the plan's smallest in-home screen size, and appliances, are serviced in the home where the plan offers in-home service; other products go to the repair depot, with shipping paid where the plan pays depot shipping.

## Evidence for each acceptance condition

| Condition | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Plan status is active | the company's record of that plan |
| Filed within the claim reporting period | the failure date as the plan holder states it on the claim, counted to the filing date |
| Failure date within the coverage dates | the failure date stated on the claim, against the coverage start and end dates on the plan record |

A plan whose status is expired, fulfilled or cancelled takes no claim.

## Claim reporting period: boundary cases (hypothetical)

Take a hypothetical claim reporting period of 30 calendar days and a failure date of 2025-08-10 (day 0).

| Claim filed on | Day count | Accepted on timing |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-09-08 | day 29 | Yes |
| 2025-09-09 | day 30 | Yes — the last day counts |
| 2025-09-10 | day 31 | No |

## Decision on the failure reported

| Failure reported | Covered when |
|---|---|
| Mechanical or electrical failure from normal use | the plan covers mechanical and electrical failure |
| Power surge | the plan covers power surge |
| Accidental drop or liquid spill | the plan covers accidental damage |
| Stain | the plan covers stains and the stain is of a type the plan lists |
| Structural failure, including a mattress body impression at least the plan's sag depth | the plan covers structural failure |
| Built-in battery below the plan's capacity threshold | the plan covers batteries |
| Display with at least the plan's dead pixel count | counts as failed |
| Any other type | denied |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A failure date one day after the coverage end date falls outside the coverage dates, whatever the filing date.
- A spill on a laptop under a plan that does not cover accidental damage is a failure of a type the plan's switches do not name, and is denied.
- A 55-inch television under a plan offering in-home service with a smallest in-home screen of 32 inches is serviced in the home; a camera under the same plan goes to the repair depot.
